Class MemoryFileSystems

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.memfs.MemoryFileSystems
public final class MemoryFileSystems extends Object
Creates file systems in memory. A file system lives until it is closed; its files are then gone. 
try (FileSystem fileSystem = MemoryFileSystems.newFileSystem()) {
    Path file = fileSystem.getPath("/work/hello.txt");
    Files.writeString(file, "Hello");
}

Each file system has a name, and its paths have URIs of the mem scheme with that name: mem://test/work/hello.txt for the path /work/hello.txt of the file system test, or mem://test/C:/work/hello.txt for C:\work\hello.txt on a Windows-style one. While the file system is open, Path.of(java.net.URI) finds its paths from such URIs, and FileSystems.getFileSystem(java.net.URI) finds it from mem://test. FileSystems.newFileSystem(java.net.URI, java.util.Map) creates one too, given its Configuration under the key "configuration", or with Configuration.unix() without it.

The file systems support the whole java.nio.file API, as the Configuration sets it up, except Path.toFile() and FileChannel.map(FileChannel.MapMode, long, long), which throw UnsupportedOperationException: neither can work on files in memory. They are thread-safe.
